messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: complex numbers?
parts:
[moved to stan-dev for general discussion]

Expose to what? Do you mean having something in
the language like:

complex a;

with some support for something like

real real_part(complex a);
real complex_part(complex a);

And then support through all the containers (matrices/vectors
and arrays) and user-defined functions.

And what about basic arithmetic operators? Other functions?

I think we could cobble together some I/O format---I don't know
if there's a usual way to do this in any of the interface
languages already.

- Bob

> On Mar 5, 2016, at 12:21 PM, Michael Betancourt <notifi...@github.com> wrote:

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: complex numbers?
parts:
On Saturday, March 5, 2016 at 2:38:03 PM UTC-5, Bob Carpenter wrote:
[moved to stan-dev for general discussion]

Expose to what?  Do you mean having something in
the language like:

  complex a;

I am thinking that

complex a;

in the Stan language would parse to

pair(double, double)

in C++ for the real and imaginary parts respectively. But any function taking a pair scalar type would have to deal with its parts separately.

I think we need to specialize the constructor so that

std::complex<stan::math::var> x;


is a compile-time error.

Ben

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] complex numbers?
parts:
It seems odd to create a specialized constructor for
a class we don't support, though if we were going to
do it anywhere, it'd be in the std lib.
